tasks.short: Work out where Noordhaven stands financially and where it is heading: margin, cash, covenant headroom, forecast.

today.trigger: Month close, the rolling forecast cycle, a board or bank question, or a large customer or contract decision.
steps: Pull the AFAS trial balance and open items into Excel
Combine them with Power BI site figures and agency flex-hour costs
Rebuild the rolling forecast and the covenant calculation
Work out the drivers (volumes, wage costs, fuel, flex mix) by hand
Write the conclusions for the management team
drudgery: Reconciling Power BI against AFAS when the figures differ
today.time_sinks: Most hours go into collecting and reconciling data before any analysis starts, plus explaining forecast misses after the fact.

lenses.faster: A nightly model built on the AFAS extract keeps the actuals, forecast and covenant ratios current, so the Director starts from a finished baseline and an AI-written variance explanation.
lenses.autonomous: When the nightly refresh lands, the model recalculates the forecast and covenant headroom and flags any driver that moves past a set threshold.
lenses.ambitious: A 13-week cash forecast and a 12-month P&L forecast for each site, updated weekly and checked against actuals, where today there is one company-wide forecast a month.
lenses.joy: No more rebuilding links and hunting for which version is right; the time goes on judgement and on talking with site managers.
lenses.options: Three to five scenarios as standard (volume loss at the largest shipper, CAO wage step, high flex share, diesel spike), each with its cash and covenant effect.
lenses.altitude: The Director stops building the forecast and owns its design: drivers, thresholds, accuracy tracking and who signs off on assumptions.
reach: FP&A Analyst: routine forecast refresh
Controller: covenant calculation for the bank

tasks.human_edge: Deciding which assumptions are credible, knowing what the business is not yet saying (a customer at risk, a site under strain), and standing behind the numbers with the board and the bank.
tasks.pattern_why: Data assembly and the scenario arithmetic can run as software, but judging the financial position and its outlook stays with the Director, who is accountable for it.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly AFAS extract refresh, plus the monthly close and the forecast calendar.
steps: Pipeline loads AFAS ledger, open items, agency hours and Rabobank balances into one model
Driver-based forecast and covenant ratios recalculate
LLM drafts a variance and outlook note citing the source lines
Director adjusts assumptions and picks the scenarios to show
Signed-off version is frozen with its assumptions log
in_practice.human_gate: The Director approves assumptions and the outlook before anything goes to the board or the bank.
data_needed: AFAS general ledger and open items
Sales volume plan by customer and site
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint forecast library with versioned assumptions and approval date

evidence.claim: Data quality is the top barrier to AI in finance (40.4% of finance executives).
Only 12% of Dutch finance professionals plan cash-in more than 30 days ahead.
Driver-based forecasting on a nightly ERP extract with LLM variance commentary is feasible with current tools.

risks: Model looks precise while the AFAS extract has mapping errors
Variance text that sounds plausible but is wrong
Forecast figures pasted into personal chatbots (shadow AI)
research_questions: How large were the forecast misses over the last 12 months, and which drivers caused them?
Is the AFAS extract clean enough per site and cost centre to drive a model without manual fixes?
Which three scenarios does the board actually ask about?

tasks.short: Assess credit limit requests for shippers and new customers, and manage the bank facility.

today.trigger: Sales brings in a new shipper or wants a higher limit; a customer goes over its limit; the bank facility is up for review.
steps: Get the request from sales by mail
Pull the KvK extract, a credit report and the customer's payment history from AFAS
Read the latest filed accounts
Decide a limit and payment terms
Set the limit in AFAS and tell sales
drudgery: Copying KvK and credit data into a template
Chasing sales for missing customer details
Re-checking limits that nobody reviewed for a year
today.time_sinks: Small requests take as much handling as large ones, and periodic limit reviews pile up.

lenses.faster: A credit file is assembled automatically from KvK, the credit report and AFAS payment behaviour, with a proposed limit and terms, so the Director reads one page and decides.
lenses.autonomous: A request, a limit breach or a credit-score drop opens a credit file and proposal on its own; requests below a set amount for limited companies go to the Credit and Collections Officer.
lenses.ambitious: Every active customer reviewed each quarter instead of only when trouble starts, and the bank facility monitored against covenants every week.
lenses.joy: No more retyping KvK data; what is left is the judgement call and the conversation with sales about the customer.
lenses.options: Three limit-and-terms options per request (lower limit, prepayment, guarantee) with the expected exposure for each.
lenses.altitude: The Director sets the credit policy, the thresholds and the rules for automatic proposals, and reviews how the limits actually perform.
reach: Credit and Collections Officer: routine limit decisions within policy
Sales: faster yes or no for prospects

tasks.human_edge: Weighing commercial value against risk, knowing the customer's story, and owning the decision. For sole-trader customers (natural persons) automated creditworthiness scoring is high-risk under the EU AI Act, so a person must decide.
tasks.pattern_why: Turning KvK extracts, credit reports and filed accounts into a structured, checkable credit proposal is an LLM step inside a fixed workflow; the approval stays human.

in_practice.trigger: New customer in AFAS, a limit increase request, a limit breach, or a credit-score change alert.
steps: Workflow pulls KvK data, credit report and AFAS payment history
LLM summarises the filed accounts and flags risks with sources
Rules engine proposes limit and terms by policy band
Director or Credit Officer approves, changes or refuses
Limit is set in AFAS with the reason recorded
in_practice.human_gate: Every limit is approved by a person; above a set amount, and for any natural-person customer, by the Director.
in_practice.logs_to: Credit file per customer in SharePoint plus the limit change log in AFAS

evidence.claim: Credit agencies sell Dutch company credit reports and scores through APIs.
Creditworthiness scoring of natural persons is a high-risk AI use.
Credit decisions and cash allocation should keep mandatory human review with timestamped logs.

risks: Automated scoring of sole traders without the AI Act safeguards
Sales pressure to rubber-stamp proposals
Stale credit data giving false comfort
research_questions: How many credit requests per month, and what share are under EUR 25k?
How many customers are sole traders (natural persons)?
Did past bad debts show warning signs in KvK or credit data that a proposal would have caught?

tasks.short: Go through the debtor aging and collection reports to see who owes what and what is overdue.

today.trigger: Weekly cash meeting and month close.
steps: Export the debtor aging from AFAS
Ask the Credit and Collections Officer for status on the large overdue items
Mark disputes and promised payments in Excel
Decide where to escalate or stop deliveries
Report DSO to the management team
drudgery: Reading aging lists line by line
today.time_sinks: Reconstructing the status of each overdue item from mail threads.

lenses.faster: A daily collection view shows aging, disputes, promises and expected cash-in per customer, with an exception list of what changed, so the review takes minutes.
lenses.autonomous: Payments from the Rabobank statement are matched, promises that are broken and limits that are breached are flagged, and dunning steps are proposed without anyone asking.
lenses.ambitious: Plan cash-in 13 weeks ahead per customer and manage DSO forward instead of explaining it afterwards.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses reading aging lists; what is left is deciding on the few customers that need a call.
lenses.options: Per problem customer: wait, call, stop delivery, payment plan or hand to a collection agency, with the expected cash effect.
lenses.altitude: The Director sets the collection policy and escalation rules and watches DSO and dispute causes, not individual invoices.
reach: Credit and Collections Officer: routine dunning runs
Sales and operations: dispute root causes such as POD and rate disputes

tasks.human_edge: Deciding when to stop deliveries to a big shipper, and calling a customer's CFO; relationships and commercial trade-offs.
tasks.pattern_why: Aging, matching, DSO and exception rules are structured and checkable; a short LLM note on disputes can sit on top.

in_practice.trigger: Daily after the CAMT.053 bank statement import and the AFAS refresh.
steps: Match bank receipts to open items in AFAS
Calculate aging, DSO and expected cash-in per customer
Flag broken promises, limit breaches and new disputes
LLM summarises dispute mail threads per customer
Director reviews the exception list in the weekly cash meeting
in_practice.human_gate: Delivery stops, write-offs and collection agency handovers need the Director's approval.
data_needed: AFAS open items and payment history
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS debtor notes and a Power BI collection dashboard with action history

evidence.claim: 81% of Dutch finance professionals explain DSO after the fact.
Credit management software automates dunning and cash-in forecasting for Dutch companies.
AR may run with people on exceptions.

risks: Wrong matching hides real overdue amounts
Automated reminders hurting key shipper relationships
Dispute notes kept outside AFAS so the picture is incomplete
research_questions: What share of receipts can be matched automatically today?
What causes most disputes (POD, rates, demurrage)?
Would the Credit and Collections Officer use an exception list instead of the full aging?

tasks.short: Prepare the board pack, annual accounts, bank covenant reports and statutory filings.

today.trigger: Month and quarter close, year end, bank reporting dates, CBS and tax deadlines.
steps: Pull the figures from AFAS after close
Build the board pack and covenant report in Excel and PowerPoint
Work with the auditor on the annual accounts
Prepare filings (KVK via SBR, CBS, tax)
Write the commentary and get sign-off
drudgery: Copying numbers into slides and Word
today.time_sinks: Copy-paste into many formats and last-minute changes that ripple through every document.

lenses.faster: Reports are generated from one locked dataset, numbers tie out automatically and an LLM drafts the commentary, so the Director edits instead of building.
lenses.autonomous: Once the close is locked, the board pack and covenant report are produced and checked against the ledger without a request.
lenses.ambitious: Be ready early for the coming B2B e-invoicing and digital reporting obligations and for CSRD if Noordhaven falls in scope, rather than a scramble.
lenses.joy: No more checking whether slide 12 matches tab 4; the time goes on the story the board needs.
lenses.options: Two or three commentary angles for the board pack (cash, margin, risk) to pick from.
lenses.altitude: The Director owns the reporting calendar, the single source of figures and the sign-off chain, and decides which reports to stop producing.
reach: Controller: first draft of statutory reports
Accountants: tie-out checks

tasks.human_edge: Legal responsibility for the accounts, judgement on disclosures and estimates, and the relationship with the auditor and the board.
tasks.pattern_why: Figures, tie-outs and formats follow fixed rules; LLM commentary is a checkable step on top, and sign-off stays human.

steps: Freeze the close dataset
Generate board pack, covenant report and filing drafts from templates
Run tie-out checks across all documents
LLM drafts commentary with links to source figures
Director edits and signs off; filings go through the SBR channel
in_practice.human_gate: Director signs every external report; statutory accounts also need the board and the auditor.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint reporting archive with version and sign-off record

evidence.claim: AFAS cannot file large-company accounts with KVK via SBR; a separate route is needed from FY2025.
B2B e-invoicing planned from 1 July 2030 and digital reporting from 1 July 2031.
CSRD applies above 1,000 employees and EUR 450 million turnover.
AI-mature teams spend more time on executive reporting, not less.

risks: Wrong commentary in a signed report
Report volume grows because it is cheap (Jevons)
Auditor cannot rebuild AI-produced workpapers
research_questions: Is Noordhaven above EUR 450 million turnover, so CSRD applies?
Which reports does the board actually read?
What does the auditor need to rely on generated reports?

tasks.short: Review how finance works (close, AP, collections, systems, controls) and propose changes.

today.trigger: Audit management letter, a missed close deadline, a control failure, or the yearly plan.
steps: Collect issues from the team, the auditor and the dashboards
Map the current process
Compare options and costs
Write a proposal for the management team
Plan the change with the team
today.time_sinks: Getting reliable facts on where the process breaks.

lenses.faster: Process data from AFAS (touchless invoice rate, close task times, audit adjustments) is analysed automatically, and an AI drafts the current-state map and options.
lenses.autonomous: Control metrics run monthly and raise an alert when a control is skipped or a KPI drifts.
lenses.ambitious: A proper finance control framework with an AI tool inventory, thresholds, logs and a named AI governance lead, ready for the auditor and the e-invoicing law.
lenses.joy: Less time arguing about anecdotes; more on designing the way the team works.
lenses.options: Several redesign options per process (AFAS configuration, add-on tool, agent with a gate) with cost and risk.
lenses.altitude: The Director becomes owner of the finance control system: which agents run, with which thresholds and logs, and who signs.
reach: Controller: control testing
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: AFAS data and integration questions

tasks.human_edge: Choosing what to change, getting the team and the works council (where jobs change) on board, and taking responsibility for controls.
tasks.pattern_why: AI speeds up analysis and drafting, but the redesign choice, change management and accountability stay with the Director.

in_practice.trigger: Monthly control metrics, audit findings or a planned improvement.
steps: Pull process metrics from AFAS and the close checklist
AI drafts the current-state map and bottlenecks
AI proposes options with cost and risk
Director chooses and discusses with team and auditor
Change and new controls logged in the control register
in_practice.human_gate: The Director decides; changes that affect jobs go past the works council.

evidence.claim: Shadow AI in accounting: give an approved tool rather than only blocking.
Finance should have an AI governance lead and timestamped logs.
66% of CFOs report comprehensive AI controls against 45% of managers.

risks: Recommendations based on bad process data
AI tools switched on by updates without review
Change fatigue in a 10-person team
research_questions: What AI tools does the finance team already use, including personal ones?
Where in the close do most days go?
What did the last management letter ask for?

tasks.short: Make operational and risk reports for management: site margins, flex costs, risks.

today.trigger: Monthly management meeting and ad hoc questions from the CEO or site managers.
steps: Pull data from AFAS, Power BI and agency portals
Build the tables and charts in Excel
Update the risk list
Write the commentary
Send the report and answer questions
drudgery: Reformatting the same data every month
today.time_sinks: Ad hoc requests that each need a new cut of the data.

lenses.faster: A standard report comes out of Power BI with LLM commentary, and managers ask follow-up questions against the same data.
lenses.autonomous: The report is produced after close and risk flags fire on thresholds (flex share, margin per site, overtime) without anyone asking.
lenses.ambitious: Weekly site margin and flex-cost reports for each site manager, done properly for the first time.
lenses.joy: No more rebuilding the same charts; the Director spends the time discussing actions with site managers.
lenses.options: Each risk shown with two or three mitigation options and their cost.
lenses.altitude: The Director decides the report set, cap and thresholds, and checks that reports lead to action.
reach: FP&A Analyst: standard reporting
Site managers: self-service answers

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which risks matter, saying uncomfortable things to management, and deciding what to act on.
tasks.pattern_why: Figures come from deterministic reports; the LLM turns them into structured commentary that can be checked against the numbers.

in_practice.trigger: Monthly close lock and threshold breaches.
steps: Power BI produces the standard report set
Rules flag threshold breaches
LLM drafts commentary and a risk summary with source references
Director reviews and edits
Report goes out with a fixed cap on pages
in_practice.human_gate: The Director approves the commentary and risk list before it goes to management.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint report archive and risk register

evidence.claim: Executive reporting takes about 32 hours a month; AI-mature teams spend more, not less.
LLM commentary on BI reports is available in mainstream tools.
evidence.source: Microsoft Copilot in Power BI (model knowledge)

risks: Report volume grows and eats the saved time
Commentary that misreads a number
Agency data arriving late or inconsistent
research_questions: Which reports lead to decisions, and which are never opened?
Can agency hours be loaded automatically from all three portals?
Do site managers want weekly figures?

tasks.short: Go through cost data to build the yearly budget and site budgets.

today.trigger: Yearly budget cycle in autumn and mid-year reforecast.
steps: Pull last year's costs from AFAS per cost centre
Collect input from site managers and HR on headcount and flex
Apply CAO wage increases, fuel and rent assumptions
Build the budget in Excel
Negotiate with the management team and finalise
today.time_sinks: Consolidation and repeated recalculation during negotiation rounds.

lenses.faster: A driver-based budget model fed from AFAS and HR data recalculates instantly, and an AI explains cost movements per site.
lenses.autonomous: Actual costs are compared with budget each month and drifts are flagged with likely causes.
lenses.ambitious: Activity-based costing per customer and per site, so pricing and budgets rest on real costs.
lenses.joy: No more consolidating 30 Excel files; the discussion is about choices.
lenses.options: Budget scenarios for CAO wage step, flex share, volume and fuel price, side by side.
lenses.altitude: The Director designs the drivers and the budget rules, and coaches site managers on their numbers.
reach: FP&A Analyst: consolidation
HR Director: headcount and flex planning

tasks.human_edge: Negotiating with site managers, making trade-offs and committing to targets.
tasks.pattern_why: AI does the analysis and recalculation; the budget choices and negotiation stay with the Director.

steps: Load AFAS costs, headcount and agency costs into the driver model
AI drafts cost analysis and budget scenarios
Site managers adjust drivers in a shared template
Director negotiates and decides
Final budget loaded into AFAS
in_practice.human_gate: The Director and management team approve the budget.

evidence.claim: Planning tools offer driver-based budgeting with AI scenario support.
Driver-based budgets on ERP cost data with AI commentary are feasible.

risks: Assumptions hidden in a model nobody understands
Site managers disengage if the model sets budgets
Bad cost centre coding distorts the analysis
research_questions: How many budget rounds does it take today and why?
Is cost centre coding in AFAS reliable enough for driver-based budgeting?
Which cost drivers explain most variance?

tasks.short: Follow diesel prices, interest rates and currency to see what they do to costs and the facility.

today.trigger: Monthly, and when diesel or interest moves sharply.
steps: Check diesel prices, Euribor and exchange rates
Compare with fuel surcharge clauses in customer contracts
Estimate the effect on margin and interest
Decide whether to adjust surcharges or hedge
Inform management
today.time_sinks: Manual data lookup and surcharge recalculation per contract.

lenses.faster: Price feeds land automatically and the effect on margin, surcharges and interest is calculated, with a short AI note.
lenses.autonomous: When diesel or rates cross a set threshold, the system calculates the surcharge change and alerts the Director and sales.
lenses.ambitious: Surcharges adjusted on time for every contract, and a clear view of interest risk on the facility.
lenses.joy: No more website lookups; the Director decides on hedging and pricing.
lenses.options: Scenarios for diesel and rate paths with surcharge and hedge options.
lenses.altitude: The Director sets the market risk policy and thresholds, and reviews whether surcharges recover costs.
reach: Sales: surcharge updates to customers
Controller: interest cost accruals

tasks.human_edge: Hedging and pricing decisions, and talks with the bank and customers.
tasks.pattern_why: Feeds and calculations are deterministic; the LLM writes a short checkable note; decisions stay human.

in_practice.trigger: Daily price feed and threshold breaches.
steps: Load diesel, Euribor and FX data
Calculate surcharge and interest effects per contract
LLM drafts a short market note
Director decides on surcharge changes or hedging
in_practice.human_gate: Surcharge changes and hedges need the Director's approval.

evidence.claim: At Noordhaven 'securities' means fuel, interest and currency.
Public diesel and rate data can be fetched automatically.

risks: Wrong feed data driving surcharge changes
Contract clauses not captured correctly
research_questions: How many contracts have fuel surcharge clauses and how are they defined?
How much margin was lost to late surcharge updates last year?
Does the facility carry floating rate exposure worth hedging?

role.altitude: From preparing and approving numbers to owning Noordhaven's finance control system: which agents and reports run, with which thresholds and logs, and who signs.
reach: FP&A Analyst: routine forecast and reporting
Credit and Collections Officer: limit decisions within policy
Controller: covenant and statutory report drafts
Sales: surcharge and credit answers
role.ceiling_note: Relationships with banks, the board, the auditor and big shippers, plus legal responsibility for the accounts, stay human. Savings are capped by AFAS data quality and by the pull to produce more reports.
skills_to_grow: EU AI Act and Dutch e-invoicing requirements
role.ambitious_version: A weekly forecast per site the business trusts, a faster close, and DSO managed forward, run on a controlled set of agents with logs the auditor can rely on.
